newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy opposition meets to consider budget boycott.
newsitem.headline: Italy opposition meets to consider budget boycott.

text.p: Leaders of Italy's opposition centre-right Freedom Alliance met on Wednesday to decide whether to continue to boycott votes in parliament on the 1997 budget.

The coalition, led by media mogul Silvio Berlusconi, refused to take part last month in sessions of the lower Chamber of Deputies which approved the 62.5 trillion lire ($40 billion) austerity package.
Alliance sources said Wednesday's meeting would decide what position to adopt in the upper Senate, where the budget is due to be debated in the full house from December 10.
The boycott began over plans by the centre-left government to seek special powers that will allow the cabinet to legislate on some areas of fiscal policy without recourse to parliament.
Parties in the ruling "Olive Tree" coalition offered what they said were concessions to the opposition on Tuesday night to try to ensure the opposition takes part in voting.
The concessions include a proposal to set up a commission of both houses of parliament to monitor the cabinet's use of any special powers on fiscal policy.
"It seems to me that in the Senate, the majority is trying to heal the wounds it inflicted in the Chamber," Francesco D'Onofrio of the centrist CCD party, part of the Berlusconi bloc, told reporters.

The opposition's lower house boycott followed a huge Freedom Alliance demonstration in Rome to protest against the budget, which is designed to help Italy make the grade for Europe's planned single currency.
